cards.explanation: The word is "difficult." On hearing it, many of His disciples said, “This is a difficult teaching. Who can accept it?” That's a lot like me staring at a new recipe and announcing, "Who can accept this much dough?"
The answer is False. Jesus does know they're grumbling. John 6:61 says He was “Aware that His disciples were grumbling about this teaching…” Then He asks them, “Does this offend you?”

The word is Spirit. Jesus says, "The Spirit gives life; the flesh profits nothing." Then He adds, "The words I have spoken to you are spirit and they are life." Life comes from the Spirit, friends, and that's what He wants them to hear.

The answer is True. The writer adds it right into the story: “For Jesus had known from the beginning which of them did not believe and who would betray Him.” So when Jesus says some of them don't believe, He isn't finding out right then. He already knew.

No one can come to Jesus unless the Father has granted it to him. Jesus says, "This is why I told you that no one can come to Me unless the Father has granted it to him." He is pointing back to something He'd said earlier. It's a heavy line, friends, so let it sit a minute.

Many of the disciples turn back and stop walking with Him. "From that time on many of His disciples turned back and no longer walked with Him." It's a heavy part of the story, and I think it's okay to just say so. They didn't wander off by accident, they turned around.
The word is Twelve. Jesus turns to the Twelve and asks, “Do you want to leave too?” Many disciples have just turned back (John 6:66), and now He puts the question straight to the Twelve.

Peter says there's nowhere else to go because Jesus has the words of eternal life. Simon Peter, one of the Twelve, says, "Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life." He doesn't list a bunch of reasons, friends. He gives one, and it's the best one.
Peter says Jesus is the Holy One of God. He says, “We believe and know that You are the Holy One of God.” He says it straight to Jesus. And notice he says both believe and know.

The answer is True. Jesus says it right after the question: "Have I not chosen you, the Twelve? Yet one of you is a devil!" It's a sobering moment, and I think it's okay to just let it be heavy. Right after Peter's strong answer, Jesus says something hard.

The writer names Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot. "He was speaking about Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot." The writer doesn't leave us guessing. I think it's a hard thing to read, friends, because Judas was in the group of the Twelve.

The word is betray. "For although Judas was one of the Twelve, he was later to betray Jesus." He was in the group, and the writer tells us what he'd do later. It's a heavy way to end this part of the story.
